plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with layered satin petals and golden centers. They bring bold color to the quiet days of mid-winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, peaking in midwinter
plants.location: Japan, the southeastern United States and the Pacific coast of North America
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that gives us tea. Camellia japonica is Japan's famous winter flower and has been cultivated there for centuries.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic, dinner-plate-sized flower head with a crown of silky pink bracts around a downy center. It blooms on the sun-baked slopes of the southern summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak flowering in late spring and summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with some blooms from late winter to autumn
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. The plant is adapted to fire, and its thick underground stems can resprout after bushfires.

plants.name: Eranthis hyemalis
plants.description: Small, buttercup-yellow cups that sit on a green ruff of leaves. They push up through frost and sometimes snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring, typically January to March
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens of Europe, including the UK, naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: The flowers close up in dull, cold weather and open wide in sunshine, so they are mostly pollinated on mild winter days by early bees.
